item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00244","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C11","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. It addresses the same Merchant Marine Act assistance regime, characterizes government benefits to the shipping industry as excessive, distinguishes legitimate support for the merchant marine from excessive aid, and directs a Cabinet officer to identify corrective action under existing law or propose legislation. The child adapts that policy and administrative framework from a particular ship subsidy to industry-wide tax benefits, requesting updated analysis and coordinated studies for legislative recommendations. C11 shares the merchant-shipping subsidy context but not this corrective machinery; C20 mentions maritime laws within a broader requested study but lacks the distinctive excessive-benefits framework.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the tax benefits now enjoyed by the shipping industry are excessive in amount","parent_excerpt":"the operator may have been offered an excessive subsidy allowance","explanation":"Both identify assistance furnished under the maritime statutory regime as excessive."},{"child_excerpt":"tax concessions are in themselves a basically unsound means of assisting the maritime industry, and ... should be replaced ... with whatever form and amount of direct aid may actually be required","parent_excerpt":"the clearly desirable objective of promoting an adequate merchant marine cannot be used to condone the allowance of excessive subsidies to individual ship operators","explanation":"Both preserve the objective of supporting the merchant marine while demanding correction of excessive or improperly structured aid."},{"child_excerpt":"I desire that the executive branch furnish the Congress with all further information needed to permit a complete correction of the present maritime tax situation","parent_excerpt":"In the event you should find it impossible to take corrective action under existing law, please consider the kind of new legislation that could be recommended for this purpose.","explanation":"Both convert the finding of excessive maritime assistance into an executive-branch assignment aimed at corrective legal or legislative action."},{"child_excerpt":"I am at the same time asking the Secretary of Commerce to undertake a study","parent_excerpt":"I would like for you to consult freely with the Secretary of Commerce, the Maritime Board, and the Comptroller General.","explanation":"Both use coordinated Cabinet and maritime-agency review to develop the corrective response."}]}
